period_note: Balance sheet is the period-end snapshot (reported); comparator column is 31.12.2010. Income-statement items are CUMULATIVE from 1 January 2011 (Jan-Mar), per the bank's own filing. CONSOLIDATED basis, NOT Solo -- this bank's interim quarterly/half-yearly filings for FY2011-FY2015(Q1) were published ONLY on a Consolidated basis (Standard Bank Limited and its subsidiaries: Standard Exchange Co. (UK) Ltd., Standard Co. (USA) Inc., SBL Capital Management Ltd., and from 2012/2013 onward Standard Bank Securities Ltd.); no separate Solo statement exists in the interim filing format used during this period (confirmed by exhaustively reading every page of each filing -- these are either a single condensed page or a short multi-page filing containing exactly one Balance Sheet/P&L, always headed 'Consolidated'). This differs from the main Q4/annual series in this dataset, which is Solo throughout. Flagged per project convention for interim/annual basis mismatches (cf. PREMIERBAN, TRUSTBANK, DHAKABANK, PRIMEBANK, ALARABANK in _HANDOFF.md). Cross-check: this quarter's own comparator column for the prior Dec-31 is Consolidated and will therefore be slightly ABOVE (not equal to) this dataset's own Solo Q4 figure for the same date -- this is expected, not an error. Source PDF's embedded text layer was corrupted (font/encoding issue, same class of defect the project found in this bank's own FY2012 annual report); re-extracted via OCR at 300dpi (pdftoppm+tesseract) instead, cross-checked digit-by-digit against the balance-sheet identity and PBT-tax=PAT, both of which reproduce exactly. EPS field was blank in the source (not stated for this quarter) and is not estimated here (project policy: never fabricate). interest_expense_cumulative is a residual (interest_income_cumulative - net_interest_income_cumulative) because the direct OCR of that single line was internally inconsistent with the rest of the statement; the residual reproduces the stated Net Interest Income exactly by construction and is the more reliable figure.
